Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by assigning each item a sequential control number, routing it through designated custodians, and preserving an immutable audit trail of approvals, dates, and signatures within bound ledgers and indexed correspondence.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted an unapproved component to the maintenance office and requested it be registered as a conforming item. The actor recorded a dated entry in the component's history file stating it had passed inspection, with a signature field attributed to a named inspector account. The actor entered a modified serial number into the aircraft technical log, replacing the original identifier with an alternate value. The actor marked the inspection record as completed on a date preceding the actual physical replacement, with a timestamp field set to an earlier value. The actor routed the paperwork through the maintenance channel, with a transmission log showing a submission entry from a named operator account. The actor appended a certification document bearing the airworthiness authority reference number, with a signature block attributed to a named authorization account. The actor updated the part traceability database, with a record field reflecting the component as received stock rather than substitute material.

3) Materials/access observed: Maintenance log (bound ledger), component history card, aircraft technical record, inspection certificate, part traceability database entry, submission transmission log, operator account credentials, authorization account credentials, inspector account credentials, component serial identifier, airworthiness reference number, date/time fields on all documents.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A dated history card entry with a signature field attributed to an inspector account, showing a conformity status prior to physical verification. An aircraft technical log entry with a serial number differing from the original component identifier, with a modification field populated by a named operator. An inspection certificate dated prior to the component replacement, with a timestamp field inconsistent with the physical event. A submission log entry in the maintenance channel showing a transmission from a named operator account at a time not matching the inspection date. A traceability database record listing the component as received stock, with a source field indicating first-article rather than substitution. A certification document with a signature block attributed to an authorization account, showing approval prior to the inspection record being filed.
